If the pain gets worse, you start coughing up blood, or you feel short of breath even when sitting still, see a doctor.

rows.user: my belly feels hard and bloated after a fizzy drink and a big meal, it comes and goes
rows.reply: This kind of bloating can happen after a heavy meal or a fizzy drink. Try resting, drinking some water, and eating smaller, lighter meals for the next day or two. If the pain becomes severe, you start vomiting, or the hardness doesn’t ease after a few days, see a doctor.

rows.user: my heart raced for a minute after 3 coffees this morning, it settled by itself and i feel fine
rows.reply: That kind of racing heart can happen after a few drinks. Take it easy for a while, sip water, and avoid more caffeine for now. If the racing heart comes back, or you feel lightheaded, sweaty, or weak, see a doctor.

rows.user: my leg starts jerking a couple of times as i'm falling asleep and then i'm fine
rows.reply: This kind of jerking is common when you're falling asleep and usually settles on its own. It's perfectly normal and doesn't need any treatment right now. Try to stay in bed or a safe place, and if you feel like it, lie on your side to help the jerking stop. If the jerking becomes much more frequent, or you notice your leg is limp or feels weak, see a doctor.

rows.user: there was a streak of blood in my phlegm this morning after a week of coughing, and none since
rows.reply: A streak of blood in your phlegm is not an emergency, but it does need a proper assessment. Please see a GP within the next 48 hours so they can check what is causing it. If you start coughing up blood repeatedly, feel short of breath, or get chest pain, go to A&E.

rows.user: i was sick once this morning and brought up a bit of yellow bile, nothing since and i've kept water down
rows.reply: That sounds like the kind of mild stomach upset that can happen after eating something heavy or spicy. Give your stomach a rest by eating nothing for the next day or two, and sip clear fluids little and often. A warm compress on your belly may help it settle. If the pain gets worse, you start vomiting repeatedly, or you feel feverish, see a doctor.

rows.user: a dull ache between my shoulder blades since i carried boxes up the stairs, better lying down
rows.reply: This kind of ache can settle on its own. Rest, put a warm compress on the area, and avoid heavy lifting for now. If the pain gets worse, you start vomiting, or you develop a fever, see a doctor.

rows.user: my vision went blurry and i felt unsteady for a few seconds when i stood up, and it's gone now
rows.reply: That is not something you need to be seen in A&E right now. Sit down, rest, and take it easy for the rest of the day. If the blurriness comes back, or you feel unsteady again, see a doctor.

rows.user: i get a bit wheezy running in cold air and it settles a few minutes after i stop
rows.reply: This kind of wheeze can happen when the air is dry or cold, and it usually settles on its own. Try wearing a scarf over your nose and mouth when you are outside, and keep your airways clear by drinking plenty of fluids. If the wheeze gets worse, you start having trouble breathing, or you feel short of breath while sitting still, see a doctor.

rows.user: i've been constipated for a couple of days but i'm still passing wind and eating normally
rows.reply: That kind of constipation can often settle on its own. Drink plenty of water, eat a light meal, and try a gentle walk. If you are not passing wind within a couple of days, or if you develop severe belly pain, vomiting, or cannot keep fluids down, see a doctor.

rows.user: i went lightheaded and nearly blacked out when i stood up too fast, i sat back down and it passed
rows.reply: That kind of lightheadedness can happen when you stand up too quickly. Sit or lie down, keep sitting still for a while, and sip water slowly. If it happens again, try sitting with your feet lower than your heart. If you pass out, get help right away.

rows.user: i hit my head on a cupboard door, there's a small bump that's sore to touch and i haven't been sick
rows.reply: A bump from hitting your head can still be serious, so you need to be assessed by a doctor today. Please contact your GP surgery and arrange to be seen within the next 48 hours.

rows.user: i get out of breath walking up two flights of stairs and i'm fine once i've got my breath back
rows.reply: That kind of breathlessness can happen when your heart is working harder than usual. It is not an emergency right now, but you should see a doctor or GP within the next 48 hours to have it assessed. If you suddenly become much more breathless than usual, or your lips or face turn blue, call an ambulance or go to A&E.

rows.user: my stools looked dark after a beetroot salad and they were back to normal today
rows.reply: That is common after a rich or dark meal. Drink plenty of water and eat lightly for the rest of the day. If the stools become black or tarry, or you start vomiting blood, go to A&E.

rows.user: my ankles swell up by the evening after a long day on my feet and they're normal again by morning
rows.reply: This kind of swelling often settles on its own. Rest your feet, elevate them when you can, and try to keep your legs straight rather than bent. A warm compress on the swollen area may help. If the swelling gets worse, you develop pain or redness, or you notice veins bulging or the skin turning discolored, see a doctor.

rows.user: my hand goes numb and tingly at night and i shake it off in the morning
rows.reply: This kind of numbness and shaking usually settles on its own. Try resting your hand and wrist at night, using a pillow or rolled-up blanket to support it, and applying a warm compress to ease the tingling. Avoid gripping things tightly at night. If the numbness lasts more than a few days, or if you start to feel weak in your hand or arm, see a doctor.

rows.user: my nose runs and i sneeze a lot after eating in the garden in spring, and my throat and chest are fine
rows.reply: That sounds like something you can manage at home for now. Rest your nose by sitting in a dry, fresh air place, and try breathing through your mouth while you breathe in. Drink plenty of fluids and avoid eating or drinking anything that smells strong. If your nose becomes blocked, or you start feeling short of breath, go to A&E.

rows.user: a dull ache under my right ribs after a very greasy takeaway, gone by the morning
rows.reply: This kind of mild ache after a heavy meal often settles on its own. Rest, sip clear fluids, and eat something light and plain for the rest of the day. Avoid rich or greasy food until it feels better. If the pain gets worse, you start vomiting, or you develop a fever, see a doctor.

rows.user: i came over hot and clammy in a stuffy meeting room, my chest was fine and it passed once i got outside
rows.reply: That sounds like something you can manage at home for now. Take it easy, stay out of stuffy places, and sip fluids. A cool shower or a cool, damp cloth on your forehead can help you feel calmer. If your chest feels tight or you get short of breath, or if you feel faint or very drowsy, go to A&E.

rows.user: my neck is stiff and sore after sleeping awkwardly, and there's no fever and no rash
rows.reply: A stiff, sore neck from sleeping can be eased with rest, a warm compress, and gentle neck stretches. Try putting a warm pad on the sore spot, avoid sleeping on your neck, and don’t strain when you wake up. If the pain gets worse, you start feeling dizzy or lightheaded, or you develop a fever, see a doctor.

rows.user: a cough and a temperature for 2 days, i'm sleeping a lot and every breath feels normal
rows.reply: A fever with a cough and feeling very tired needs to be assessed by a doctor today. Please contact your GP surgery now and ask for an appointment today. If you start feeling short of breath, get chest pain, or feel confused, go to A&E instead.

rows.user: i'm 10 weeks pregnant and getting mild stretching twinges low down in my belly, and there's no bleeding
rows.reply: I can't judge how serious this is from what you've described. Because it involves pregnancy, I'm not able to triage it for you. Please see a doctor or GP for an assessment.

rows.user: my left arm aches because i slept on it funny, and i get pins and needles when i lift it overhead
rows.reply: This sounds like something you can manage at home for now. Rest your arm and wrist, avoid putting it on your chest or over your heart, and don’t lift it overhead until it feels better. If the pain gets worse, you develop weakness in your arm or leg, or you lose feeling in your hand or arm, see a doctor.

rows.user: my toddler is grizzly and clingy with a cold but he wakes up fine and is drinking
rows.reply: A young child who is grumpy and clingy with a cold can be hard to manage, but it is not an emergency. Keep offering him plenty of fluids, let him rest, and try gentle, calm reassurance rather than forcing him to do anything. If he becomes unusually drowsy, hard to wake, or does not drink enough, see a doctor.

rows.user: i snore and sometimes wake myself up, but i can breathe fine lying down in the day
rows.reply: That kind of snoring and waking up can be annoying and uncomfortable, but it doesn’t need emergency care right now. Try sleeping on your side, using a pillow to prop yourself up, and avoiding alcohol or lying flat before bed. If you start having trouble breathing while you sleep, or if you feel short of breath when you wake up, see a doctor.

rows.user: loose stools since a takeaway last night, but i'm keeping water down and weeing normally
rows.reply: Loose stools after a rich meal can settle on its own. Keep sipping clear fluids, rest, and eat small bland meals for a day or two. If you start vomiting, can't keep fluids down, or feel faint, go to A&E.

rows.user: i notice the odd extra beat when i'm lying in bed at night, no chest pain and no breathlessness
rows.reply: That is something that can happen to many people, especially when they are resting. Try putting a warm compress on your chest, taking a warm bath, or doing gentle breathing exercises before bed. Avoid lying flat on your back for a while, and if you feel faint or lightheaded, sit upright and stay upright until you feel better. If the extra beat becomes constant, you get chest pain, or you faint, go to A&E.

rows.user: a headache behind my eyes at the end of a long day at the screen, better after a break
rows.reply: This kind of headache often settles with a short break. Sit in a quiet place, rest your eyes, and take a few minutes to breathe slowly. If the headache becomes severe, you get a stiff neck, or you feel confused, go to A&E.

rows.user: food went down the wrong way at lunch and i coughed for a minute and then it cleared
rows.reply: That sounds like something you can manage at home for now. Take it easy, sip fluids slowly, and avoid eating or drinking anything heavy or very hot until your throat feels settled. If you start to feel short of breath, get chest pain, or the cough lasts longer than a few days, see a doctor.

rows.user: my 3 year old swallowed a small smooth plastic bead, she's eating and drinking and isn't bothered by it
rows.reply: This is not an emergency right now. Have her eat and drink normally, and keep an eye on her. If she starts vomiting, becomes hard to wake, or you see the bead in her vomit, call an ambulance or go to A&E.

rows.user: my chest muscles are sore today after doing press ups for the first time in years
rows.reply: That kind of soreness after doing something you haven’t done in a while is common. Rest, take it easy, and gradually build up the exercise over the next few days. If the pain gets worse, you start feeling short of breath, or you get chest pain that doesn’t go away, see a doctor.

rows.user: i lose my words and my train of thought when i'm exhausted and it sorts itself out after a good sleep
rows.reply: This kind of thing can happen to anyone, and it is not something I can judge from what you have described. Please see a doctor or GP so they can assess it properly.

rows.user: my legs are stiff and achy after a long haul flight, both the same, and it eased off after a walk
rows.reply: That kind of leg stiffness and aching after a long flight is common and usually settles on its own. Rest, take a warm shower or hot water bottle on the legs, and try gentle walking or a gentle leg stretch. It should ease over the next few days. If the pain becomes severe, you develop weakness or numbness in your legs, or you notice a limp, see a doctor.

rows.user: my belly twinges when i cough because i pulled something lifting at work, and there's no temperature
rows.reply: That kind of belly ache can happen after a sudden strain. Take it easy for a day or two, drink plenty of fluids, and avoid heavy lifting or straining. A warm compress on the area may help it settle. If the pain gets worse, you start vomiting, or you develop a fever, see a doctor.

rows.user: i was sick after a dodgy takeaway and my chest burns from the acid, a glass of water helped
rows.reply: This sounds like the kind of stomach upset that can settle on its own. Give your stomach a rest by eating nothing for the next day or two, and sip small sips of water or clear fluids often. A warm compress on your belly may help the burning feel better. If the pain gets worse, you start vomiting repeatedly, or you feel faint or dizzy, see a doctor.

rows.user: my foot gets pins and needles if i sit cross legged too long and it comes back after a minute of walking
rows.reply: This kind of tingling or numbness can happen when your blood flow is restricted, especially if you sit cross-legged for a long time. It usually settles on its own. Try sitting upright, moving around, and putting a small rolled-up sock or a small elastic band around your foot to help the blood flow. If the numbness lasts more than a few minutes, or you get weakness or pain in your foot, go to A&E.

rows.user: my little boy has a barking cough at night but he's running about happily and breathing normally
rows.reply: A baby who is otherwise active and breathing normally with a barking cough at night can often be managed at home. Keep the room calm and quiet, and try a cool-mist humidifier or a steamy shower to help settle the cough. If he starts to breathe faster, seems to struggle to breathe, or his lips or face turn blue, call an ambulance or go to A&E.

rows.user: i was sick twice last night and feel washed out today but i'm keeping fluids down
rows.reply: That sounds like it could be a mild case of something you had before. Rest, sip fluids little and often, and avoid anything heavy or rich until you feel better. If you start feeling confused, have a stiff neck, or the pain gets worse, see a doctor.

rows.user: burning in the middle of my chest after a big spicy curry, worse when i lie down and milk settles it
rows.reply: This kind of burning chest pain often settles when you lie flat and you can drink milk. Try sitting up, sipping small amounts of milk, and avoiding rich or spicy food for a day or two. If the pain gets worse when you lie down, or you start feeling short of breath, go to A&E.

rows.user: my dad has been forgetful and a bit vague after a bad night's sleep but he knows where he is and he's eating
rows.reply: That kind of memory change can happen after a poor night's sleep and often settles on its own. Have him rest in a quiet, calm place, keep his meals regular, and try to help him sleep better by keeping the room cool and dark. If he starts forgetting where he put his glasses, becomes confused about the time, or is hard to wake, that is a sign he needs to be assessed.

rows.user: i got out of breath carrying the shopping and my heart pounded, back to normal in a couple of minutes
rows.reply: That kind of breathlessness can happen when you are carrying extra weight or doing something you are not used to. Take it easy for a while, rest, and sip water. If you start feeling short of breath while sitting still, or your chest feels tight, or you get chest pain, see a doctor.

rows.user: there's a soft lump in my groin that pops out when i lift something and goes back in when i lie down
rows.reply: This kind of lump can be caused by a small hernia or a cyst that moves with activity. It is not an emergency, but it should be assessed by a doctor. Please see a GP or doctor within the next 48 hours.

rows.user: my heart flutters for a second when i'm stressed at work and then it's gone and i carry on
rows.reply: That kind of fluttering is common when your heart is on edge, and it usually settles on its own. Try taking a few minutes to breathe slowly and calmly, and if you feel faint or lightheaded, sit down and rest until it passes. If the fluttering comes with chest pain, you feel faint, or you faint, go to A&E.
